title: Jet representations from a rational action along a fixed section
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $X$ be an integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-pc-scheme]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Products are scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be a nonempty dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], with an action $a:G\times_kY\to Y$, namely a morphism satisfying the unit and multiplication identities. Let $\alpha:G\times_kX\dashrightarrow X$ be its rational extension, a rational map meaning an equivalence class of morphisms on dense opens, with its largest domain $D$. Suppose $P\in X(k)$, $(e,P)\in D$, and $\alpha|_{V\times_k\{P\}}$ is the constant morphism with value $P$, where $V=\{g:(g,P)\in D\}$. Then $D$ contains $G\times_k\{P\}$ and $\alpha|_{G\times_k\{P\}}=P\circ p_G$. Write $R=\mathcal O_{X,P}$ for the stalk of the structure sheaf, $\mathfrak m=\ker(R\to k)$ for its maximal ideal, and $Q_n=R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ for $n\geq1$, with ordinary ideal powers and quotient rings [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Each $Q_n$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional $k$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. The canonical map $i_n:X_n=\operatorname{Spec}Q_n\to X$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The restriction of $\alpha$ to $G\times_kX_n\subseteq D$ factors through $i_n$ and defines an action $a_n:G\times_kX_n\to X_n$. Its inverse pullback gives a homomorphism $\rho_n:G\to\operatorname{GL}(Q_n)$, where the general linear group is [def-sc-general-linear-group] after choosing a basis, and $\rho_n(B)(g)$ is an algebra automorphism of $B\otimes_kQ_n$ for each commutative $k$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The quotient maps $Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$ intertwine these representations. The scheme-theoretic kernels $K_n=G\times_{\operatorname{GL}(Q_n),\rho_n,e}\operatorname{Spec}k$ are closed finite-type subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and $K_{n+1}\subseteq K_n$. No faithfulness assumption, smoothness of $X$, or affineness of $G$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-point-thickenings-base-change] to $(X,P)$. Its hypotheses are precisely separatedness, finite type and a rational point, without smoothness of $X$. Thus $P$ is closed, its ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$ defines $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}Q_n$ by $\mathcal J^{n+1}$, and $Q_n$ is nonzero finite-dimensional. For every $k$-scheme $T$, the section in $T\times X$ has ideal $\mathcal J_T$, and its $(n+1)$st power defines $T\times X_n$. These identifications and the surjections $Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$ are compatible with every base change.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, p.150, local quotients and base change; Stacks 04EY (definition-first-order-infinitesimal-neighbourhood), 04EZ (lemma-first-order-infinitesimal-neighbourhood).

proof.text: We will compare maps on opens of $T\times X$, for $T=G^r$ and also $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The open $T\times Y$ is scheme-theoretically dense there. Indeed, on a chart $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_k A)$ with $A$ a domain, choose a nonempty principal $D(f)\subseteq Y\cap\operatorname{Spec}A$. The injection $A\to A_f$ remains injective after tensoring with $B$: choose a $k$-basis of $B$, so this is a direct sum of copies of that injection. Thus a function vanishing on $T\times Y$ vanishes on the chart. This sheaf injection restricts to every open. By [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated], two maps from any such open into the separated $k$-scheme $X$ agreeing on $T\times Y$ are equal. In particular $D$ contains $G\times Y$ with restriction $a$: this morphism is a representative of $\alpha$, and any other representative agrees on overlaps by the same argument. Their union therefore glues to the maximal representative. For $g\in G(k)$ write $D_g=\{x:(g,x)\in D\}$ and $f_g=\alpha(g,-):D_g\to X$; it restricts to the automorphism $a(g,-)$ on $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, rational action on the completion; explicit affine density calculation. Stacks 01RH (morphisms-lemma-equality-of-morphisms), 0A1Y (lemma-rational-map-from-reduced-to-separated).

proof.text: The scheme $G$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], and is nonempty and connected. Hence [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] makes $G$ integral, in particular irreducible. The open $V=\{g:(g,P)\in D\}$ contains $e$. For each $g\in G(k)$ the opens $V$ and $gV^{-1}$ intersect, by irreducibility. Their intersection is smooth and nonempty, so [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] supplies $u\in(V\cap gV^{-1})(k)$. Write $v=u^{-1}g\in V(k)$, so $g=uv$. This uses translations and inversion as scheme automorphisms, directly from the group-object identities; it requires no affineness of $G$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, rational-action variant; agent expansion of the fixed-section continuation. Stacks 056S (lemma-smooth-regular), 0569, 033N underpin the cited regularity and integrality inputs.

proof.text: For these $u,v$, consider the open $E\subseteq G\times X$ defined by $(u^{-1}h,x)\in D$ and $\alpha(u^{-1}h,x)\in D_u$. On $E$ the formula $F(h,x)=f_u(\alpha(u^{-1}h,x))$ is a morphism. It is defined at $(g,P)$, since $u,v\in V$ and $f_v(P)=P=f_u(P)$ by the hypothesis. On $E\cap(G\times Y)$ it equals $a(h,x)$ by the action identity. By step 2 this is a representative of $\alpha$, so maximality gives $E\subseteq D$ and $F=\alpha|_E$. Thus $g\in V$ for every $g\in G(k)$. If $G\setminus V$ were nonempty, [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] would supply a closed point of $G$ in it; [lem-kun-closed-point-field] makes its residue field finite over $k$, hence equal to the algebraically closed field $k$. This contradicts $G(k)\subset V$. Therefore $V=G$, so $G\times\{P\}\subseteq D$ and the assumed equality along $V\times\{P\}$ is now the asserted equality along the whole section.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154: omitted local-action details, supplied here by translating representatives. Stacks 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), 01RH for the comparison.

proof.text: Over $G$ define $C(g,x)=(g,\alpha(g,x))$ on $D$, and $C^-(g,x)=(g,\alpha(g^{-1},x))$ on $D^-=\{(g,x):(g^{-1},x)\in D\}$. Both domains contain the whole section and both maps fix it as a morphism. Put $N=D\cap C^{-1}(D^-)$ and $M=D^-\cap(C^-)^{-1}(D)$. On $N$, the composite $C^-C$ is the identity: on $G\times Y$ this is the original action law, and step 2 extends the equality. Likewise $CC^-=\mathrm{id}$ on $M$. These equations imply $C(N)\subseteq M$, $C^-(M)\subseteq N$, and make $C:N\to M$ an isomorphism with inverse $C^-$. Both opens contain the whole section. An isomorphism fixing a closed section identifies the kernels of restriction to that section, so $C$ identifies $\mathcal J_G|_M$ with $\mathcal J_G|_N$, and likewise every power. This is an equality of ideals, not merely of their radicals.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, p.150, action on local quotients, adapted to the rational action of Proposition 8.25 by the explicitly displayed mutually inverse open maps; Stacks 01RH.

proof.text: The topological support of $G\times X_n$ is exactly the section, since its defining ideal is $\mathcal J_G^{n+1}$. It consequently factors through both open subschemes $N,M$, hence through $D$; factoring through an open uses only containment of the topological image. Step 5 identifies its ideal on $N,M$, so restricts $C$ to an automorphism $C_n$ of $G\times X_n$ over $G$. Its second component is $a_n$, and $i_na_n=\alpha(1_G\times i_n)$. The identity law holds since $f_e=\mathrm{id}$ wherever defined by step 2. For the multiplication law, on the open of $G\times G\times X$ where both composites are defined, $\alpha(g,\alpha(h,x))$ and $\alpha(gh,x)$ agree by step 2 and the action law on $Y$. This open contains the entire section, hence $G\times G\times X_n$. Restricting the equality and using that $i_n$ is a monomorphism gives $a_n(g,a_n(h,z))=a_n(gh,z)$ as morphisms, including nilpotents. Thus $a_n$ is an action.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, p.150, infinitesimal actions; Stacks 04EZ (lemma-first-order-infinitesimal-neighbourhood), explicit ideal-power restriction and rational-action identities.

proof.text: For any $k$-scheme $T$ and $h:T\to G$, the action of $h$ on $T\times X_n$ is a $T$-automorphism $c_h$, inverse $c_{h^{-1}}$. Its inverse pullback $T_h=c_{h^{-1}}^*$ acts on the free sheaf $\mathcal O_T\otimes_k Q_n$. In a basis of $Q_n$ it is an invertible matrix of sections of $\mathcal O_T$. By [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] and the coordinate description in [def-sc-general-linear-group], this is a $T$-point of $\operatorname{GL}(Q_n)$. The construction commutes with all pullbacks $T'\to T$. By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], on the category of $k$-schemes it therefore gives a morphism $\rho_n:G\to\operatorname{GL}(Q_n)$. Since $c_{(hh')^{-1}}=c_{h'^{-1}}c_{h^{-1}}$, contravariance gives $T_{hh'}=T_hT_{h'}$ and $T_1=1$; thus it is a group-scheme homomorphism. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, step 1 identifies its underlying algebra with $B\otimes_kQ_n$, and $T_h$ is a $B$-algebra automorphism, not just a linear map.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, p.150, natural representations on local quotients; Stacks 001P (categories-lemma-yoneda), 01I1 (schemes-lemma-morphism-into-affine).

proof.text: Both restrictions to $X_n$ and $X_{n+1}$ come from the same open isomorphism $C$, which preserves both ideal powers. Hence inverse pullback commutes with $Q_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow Q_n$, also after every scalar extension. By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], $K_n$ is a closed subgroup with $K_n(B)=\ker\rho_n(B)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $B$. It is finite type: on a finite affine cover of the finite-type scheme $G$, its coordinate rings are quotients of finitely generated $k$-algebras. If $h\in K_{n+1}(B)$, compatibility and the surjectivity of $B\otimes Q_{n+1}\to B\otimes Q_n$ give $\rho_n(h)=1$. Apply this to the universal points on affine charts of $K_{n+1}$; their induced maps to $K_n$ agree on overlaps by the closed-immersion monomorphism. They glue to $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ over $G$, which is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion]. This proves the descending assertion scheme-theoretically.
